about: Road rulebook, stage 1 (Nov 22 2026). The written rules are the Claude Doc 'Road rulebook (stage 1)'; this file carries the same numbers and the measures the road code and the stage 2 checker both read. Lengths in metres, speeds in mph.

rules.text: Roads are built from the map in class order; the route does not come first.
A road is never moved, bent or narrowed by a lower road joining it.
Tarmac, lines and signs are the same with or without a route.
The higher road keeps the map's line through a junction: straight where the map is straight.
One priority road per junction; never give way on every arm.
Give-way line on every minor arm of a priority junction.
The give-way line's nearer edge continues the major road's edge, at any angle; never set back.
Give-way line across the approach lane only; the other half a 1009A broken edge line.
Whole-width give-way line where the lane's would be under 2.75 m, or the minor road is one-way.
Give-way triangle mid-lane, leading edge 2.1 to 2.75 m from the line (15 m at most).
GIVE WAY sign at A/trunk roads, crossroads and turning priority; left side, about 1.5 m before the line, 12 m at most.
No give-way marking at private accesses or quiet residential streets.
STOP line and sign only where visibility along the major road is short.
Unmarked junctions (nobody has priority) carry no line and no sign.
A minor road meets the major road square, with a sharp turn at the line.
The major road's centre line runs on through the junction as a warning line.
The major road's solid edge line is not carried across a side road's mouth.
A side road's kerbside lines stop where its kerb turns the corner.
Corner kerbs rounded; the rounding never crosses another road.
rules.source: DMRB CD 123 / Manual for Streets (to read)

rules.text: Junction warning line on the major road.
Warning line on the minor road too, none where the give-way line is whole-width.
Crossroads and staggered junctions marked like Ts.
Centre line by speed limit.
No centre line under 5.5 m wide.
Centre line in the geometric middle unless moved for parking.
Warning line in place of the centre line before junctions, roundabouts and blind stretches.
Lane lines by speed limit, never wider than the centre line.
Edge line 1012.1, about 0.225 m in from the edge.
Double white lines where overtaking visibility is too short.
Double yellow lines along kerbs near town junctions.
Clockwise round every roundabout.
Each entry gives way to the right: one broken line 1003.1.
Roundabout approaches carry warning lines.
Mini roundabouts: white disc, three arrows, give-way 1003.3; island under about 4 m.
Splitter islands at entries; chevrons and signs on every ring.
Warning sign distance before the hazard by speed.
Warning sign height by speed.
Warning lines and signs only for hazards that are unusual or not obvious.
STOP sign never alone, never on all arms, 1.5 m before its line, 6 m at most.
Signs face their traffic, on the left unless blocked.
Speed limits change only at signs.
Keep left.
Never against a one-way street.
Round roundabouts clockwise, leaving by an exit.
No banned turns, no roads closed to motorbikes.
Join a major road at the give-way line with a sharp turn; leave it from the correct side.
Cross a dual carriageway in two halves where the reservation is deep enough.
Sat nav instructions describe the turn actually made.

exceptions.text: Chevrons and signs on every roundabout.
Country roads: tarmac straight to the grass verge.
Lines painted into the road material.
Pub signs on buildings only; made-up shop names.
Forgiving kerbs; kerbed roundabout islands allowed.
